proof.criterion: An unclaimed role's handover over a cursor no read can decode ends at once, reports nothing at Error, and leaves nothing behind (item 2, first half).
proof.surface: A real listener process on a real NATS; an undecodable cursor written straight onto notifications.envoy.kept.cursor.<role>, which is a stored subject of the listener's own, then 200 keeps against that role.
proof.observed: 200 keeps took 9243 ms in total, 46 ms each, which is the publish's own cost and no retry window; 0 ERROR lines across the whole run; the listener's threads went 7 -> 8 and its RSS 28176 -> 34524 kB, which is 200 stream publishes rather than accumulation. At the old head one such handover alone costs 3.40 s of retries.
proof.negativeControl: The same binary retries and reports for a role whose cached claim names a session, which is the other half of the rule; and the old head's 3.40 s failure is the before-measurement for this same cursor.
proof.limitOfThisMeasurement: The listener exposes no go_goroutines metric and no pprof endpoint, so I could not count goroutines directly and do not claim to have. What I measured is what a parked handover would show from outside: it holds the role's guard, so the keeps behind it would slow or stall, and a process collecting them would grow threads and RSS. None of the three moved. The guard's give-up itself is pinned by the unit test above.

proof.criterion: A claimed role whose holder resolution fails retries and reports at Error (item 2, second half).
proof.surface: The unit test TestAHandoverOfAClaimedRoleRetriesAHolderResolutionThatFailed, red at a4b9ededf432 and green here.
proof.observed: FAIL 0.04 s at a4b9ededf432 with the handoff's message (a resolution that did not answer read as a role nobody holds); passes here.
proof.negativeControl: The unclaimed half above, which must NOT retry, measured live at 46 ms a keep: the same rule read from both sides.
proof.notDrivenLive: I did not drive this half on the real stack and did not pretend to. Making a holder resolution FAIL live needs the session bucket read to error, which means stopping NATS under the listener - and that stops the keeps that start the handover too, so the rig cannot isolate the failing resolution from a dead bus. The unit test is the isolation.
